| - | - | - |
| **Upper Belvedere** | Klimt, Schiele, palace rooms | Yes, must-see |
| **Lower Belvedere** | Temporary exhibitions, baroque interiors | Only if you’re into the current exhibition |
| **Belvedere 21** | Modern art & architecture | Skip unless you have free entry or love contemporary art |

…

[Vienna Belvedere Palace: Which Museum Should You Visit? > Tips for Visiting > Ticket Tips]

- Tickets can be bought **online** or **directly at the entrance** of each museum.
- **Combination tickets** are available for:
- Upper + Lower Belvedere
- All three locations (Upper, Lower, and Belvedere 21)
- All locations are included in the **Vienna Pass** and the **Bundesmuseen Card**.
- The Upper Belvedere and Belvedere 21 are included with the **NÖ Card**, but you’ll need to collect a physical ticket at the ticket office.

…

[Vienna Belvedere Palace: Which Museum Should You Visit? > Tips for Visiting > General Tips]

- **Arrive early** to avoid tour group crowds, especially at the Upper Belvedere.
- **Check exhibition schedules** before visiting Lower Belvedere or Belvedere 21, it really determines whether it’s worth going.
- **Don’t skip the gardens**, they’re beautiful, free, and open year-round.
- **No-photo signs**: Some artworks (especially on the second floor of Upper Belvedere) are marked as no photography, please respect those.
- **Allow enough time**: About 2 hours for the Upper Belvedere, and 60 minutes for the others.
- For a unique coffee spot, visit the nearby **Aufzug Café**, where you can sip your espresso inside an old elevator box, much more memorable than the museum café."],"code":"SUCCESS"}}],"query":"Upper Belvedere visit Museum Ludwig Kunstsammlung K20 K21 official 2026","cache_metadata":{"status":"miss","age_ms":0},"request_id":"ed7eae67-84b6-49db-86a1-a9c68b15453b"}

No timed-entry tickets are required for the permanent collections at K20 and K21 or for most special exhibitions. Time-slot tickets are required for “Franz Marc” and “Playground”. These can be presented either digitally or in printed form.

All admission tickets (except time-slot tickets and special offer tickets) are valid for one year from the date of purchase and entitle the holder to one admission to K20 or K21. We accept digital and printed tickets. Due to different visitor flows, there may be waiting times even with an online ticket.

results.title: Vienna Belvedere Palace: Which Museum Should You Visit?
results.description: Honest guide to Vienna’s Belvedere Palace, what to see, which museum is worth it, and how to plan your visit like a local.

highlights:
[Vienna Belvedere Palace: Which Museum Should You Visit? > What Is the Belvedere Palace?]

| Location | What You’ll See | Worth Visiting? |
| - | - | - |
| **Upper Belvedere** | Klimt, Schiele, palace rooms | Yes, must-see |
| **Lower Belvedere** | Temporary exhibitions, baroque interiors | Only if you’re into the current exhibition |
| **Belvedere 21** | Modern art & architecture | Skip unless you have free entry or love contemporary art |

…

[Vienna Belvedere Palace: Which Museum Should You Visit? > Tips for Visiting > Ticket Tips]

- Tickets can be bought **online** or **directly at the entrance** of each museum.
- **Combination tickets** are available for:
- Upper + Lower Belvedere
- All three locations (Upper, Lower, and Belvedere 21)
- All locations are included in the **Vienna Pass** and the **Bundesmuseen Card**.
- The Upper Belvedere and Belvedere 21 are included with the **NÖ Card**, but you’ll need to collect a physical ticket at the ticket office.

…

[Vienna Belvedere Palace: Which Museum Should You Visit? > Tips for Visiting > General Tips]

- **Arrive early** to avoid tour group crowds, especially at the Upper Belvedere.
- **Check exhibition schedules** before visiting Lower Belvedere or Belvedere 21, it really determines whether it’s worth going.
- **Don’t skip the gardens**, they’re beautiful, free, and open year-round.
- **No-photo signs**: Some artworks (especially on the second floor of Upper Belvedere) are marked as no photography, please respect those.
- **Allow enough time**: About 2 hours for the Upper Belvedere, and 60 minutes for the others.
- For a unique coffee spot, visit the nearby **Aufzug Café**, where you can sip your espresso inside an old elevator box, much more memorable than the museum café.
